sources.page_snippet: Karolina Muchova put up a spirited fight in her first Grand Slam final, taking world No. 1 and defending champion Iga Swiatek to three sets.Karolina Muchova put up a spirited fight in her first Grand Slam final, taking world No. 1 and defending champion Iga Swiatek to three sets, 6-2 5-7 6-4, in Paris and impressing the crowd with her incredible game. Swiatek holds off stirring Muchova fightback to win French Open · “At two-love up, I felt like she got a little tentative in those few games,” said Chris Evert, who was calling the match. “I think Karolina [Muchova] played better when she was behind, she played with freedom, played with power, but as soon as she was ahead, she wanted to protect her lead and got a little tentative.” Eurosport’s Mats Wilander went even further, after watching Muchova mix it up in the final with a variety of powerful groundstrokes, slice backhands and impeccably placed volleys that had Swiatek on the run on numerous occasions. Muchova had already garnered plenty of headlines after taking out one of the big favourites, Aryna Sabalenka, in the semi-finals and many were wondering how she would recover physically from that gruelling match on Thursday.
